questions.stem: Which three substances are prescribed pollutants for the purpose of CSA 2001 s. 187 under VPDCR s. 4?
options: Oil and oily mixtures, garbage, and organotin biocides
questions.explanation: VPDCR s. 4 prescribes oil and any oily mixture, garbage, and organotin compounds that act as biocides. Sewage and greywater have their own rules but are not on the s. 4 list.

questions.stem: What does CSA 2001 s. 187 say about discharging a prescribed pollutant?
options: It is allowed if the master approves
It is allowed in small quantities
No person or vessel may do so except as the regulations (or a permit) allow
It is allowed anywhere beyond 3 nautical miles from shore
questions.explanation: Section 187 is a general ban with exceptions only as set out in the regulations or a permit under CEPA 1999. There is no general small-quantity allowance.

questions.stem: Which of these is an excuse for a discharge under VPDCR s. 5?
options: The discharge was small and nobody was watching
Discharge necessary to save lives, secure the vessel's safety or prevent its immediate loss
The crew did not have time to land the waste
questions.explanation: Section 5(a) excuses a discharge needed to save lives, secure safety or prevent immediate loss. Convenience, schedule or size are not excuses.

questions.stem: A vessel is damaged in a grounding that is an accident of navigation and some oil leaks. When is the discharge NOT excused under s. 5(b)?
options: When the vessel is under 12 m
When the accident resulted from an action outside the ordinary practice of seafarers
questions.explanation: Section 5(b) excuses discharge from damage in an accident of navigation unless the accident occurs as a result of an action outside the ordinary practice of seafarers.

questions.stem: A master learns that fuel may be leaking into the harbour. Under CSA 2001 s. 186.3(2), what must the master do?
options: Wait for the harbour authority to act
Take reasonable measures to protect the marine environment, including eliminating the risk if feasible, and notify the authorized representative if Canadian
Move the vessel to another berth only
Record it in the log and do nothing else
questions.explanation: Section 186.3(2) requires reasonable measures, including eliminating the risk if feasible, and the master of a Canadian vessel notifies the authorized representative unless the risk has been eliminated.

questions.stem: Bilge water may be discharged under VPDCR s. 30 or 31 only if it passes through filtering equipment that produces effluent of what oil content, and the vessel is in what status?
options: 100 ppm or less, and the vessel is moored
50 ppm or less, at any time
1 ppm or less, only at anchor
15 ppm or less, and the vessel is en route
questions.explanation: Both sections require the vessel to be en route and the equipment to produce undiluted effluent of not more than 15 ppm, with no chemicals added to defeat detection.

questions.stem: In the inland waters of Canada, at what oil content must the alarm and discharge-stopping device act under s. 30(1)(c)(iii)?
questions.explanation: Clause (A) sets 5 ppm for inland waters; clause (B) sets 15 ppm for other Section I waters.

questions.stem: A 9 m workboat has no oil filtering equipment. Based on VPDCR ss. 30 and 31, what is the position on discharging oily bilge water?
options: It may be pumped overboard beyond 3 nautical miles
It may be pumped overboard if the engine is running
The authorizations require filtering equipment, so there is no authorization to discharge it and it should be kept for shore disposal
It may be pumped overboard if diluted with soap
questions.explanation: Each authorization depends on oil filtering equipment producing 15 ppm or less, and s. 187 bans anything not authorized. Adding chemicals to evade detection is itself excluded by s. 30(1)(d) and s. 31(1)(d).

questions.stem: Where VPDCR s. 101 allows it, how far from the nearest land must floating, non-plastic dunnage or packing material be discharged?
questions.explanation: Section 101(1)(a) sets 25 nautical miles for floating non-plastic dunnage, lining or packing; 12 applies to other non-plastic garbage; 3 applies to ground garbage.

questions.stem: Food scraps ground so they pass a screen with openings of 25 mm or less may be discharged, where s. 101 applies, at what distance from the nearest land?
questions.explanation: Section 101(1)(c) sets 3 nautical miles for garbage passed through a comminuter or grinder to a screen of 25 mm or less.

questions.stem: Which of the following garbage items is covered by an authorized-discharge distance in VPDCR s. 101(1)?
options: None of these; plastics are not covered by any distance
questions.explanation: Section 101(1) covers dunnage, non-plastic garbage, ground non-plastic garbage and cargo residues. Plastics are excluded from paragraph (b) and have no distance at which discharge is authorized.

questions.stem: At what overall length must a vessel display placards about garbage discharge under VPDCR s. 103?
questions.explanation: Section 103(1) applies to every vessel 12 m or more in length overall. The 400 GT and 15 person thresholds apply to the garbage management plan and Record Book.

questions.stem: Which vessel must keep a Garbage Record Book under VPDCR s. 105?
options: One certified to carry 15 persons or more (unless it only makes voyages of an hour or less)
questions.explanation: Section 105(1) applies to vessels of 400 GT or more or certified for 15 persons or more; s. 105(2) excludes a 15-person vessel that only engages on voyages of one hour or less.

questions.stem: A 12 m vessel certified for 12 persons is in Section II waters outside any designated sewage area. Treated sewage from its marine sanitation device (comminuted and disinfected) may be discharged at what minimum distance from shore under s. 96(1)(e)(i)?
questions.explanation: A vessel under 400 GT and certified for no more than 15 persons has the 1 nautical mile option for comminuted and disinfected sewage, or 3 nautical miles while en route at the fastest feasible speed.

questions.stem: What fecal coliform count must sewage effluent meet when discharged through a marine sanitation device in a designated sewage area?
questions.explanation: Section 96(1)(b) sets 14/100 mL in a designated sewage area; s. 96(1)(a) sets 250/100 mL elsewhere.

questions.stem: What does VPDCR s. 131.1(4) require about greywater?
options: The release must not deposit solids in the water or leave a sheen
Greywater is limited to 10 litres per hour
Greywater must be kept for 30 days
questions.explanation: Section 131.1(4) forbids solids and a sheen. The extra marine sanitation device or 3 nautical mile rule applies only to new passenger vessels carrying more than 500 passengers.

questions.stem: Under VPDCR s. 132, a master must report which of these to a marine safety inspector or MCTS officer?
options: An anticipated discharge that would be prohibited, as well as an actual one
Only discharges that have been confirmed by a laboratory
questions.explanation: Section 132(1) covers discharges and anticipated discharges that are prohibited or are authorized under s. 5(a), (b), (d) or (e). There is no volume threshold.

questions.stem: A master is busy keeping the vessel off a lee shore when a fuel leak starts. When must the report be made under s. 132(3)?
options: Only at the end of the voyage
As soon as feasible after the leak, once the master is free from saving the vessel
Never, because the leak is excused
questions.explanation: Section 132(3)(b) allows the report to follow as soon as feasible if the master is busy with saving lives, securing safety, or limiting damage. An excuse under s. 5(a) does not remove the reporting duty.

questions.stem: Which item must a discharge report include under s. 132(5)?
options: The identity of every vessel involved, date, time and location, nature and estimated quantity, and the assistance or salvage measures
questions.explanation: Section 132(5) lists vessel identity, time and place, nature and quantity of the pollutant, and for a discharge the assistance and salvage measures used.

questions.stem: The maximum penalty on summary conviction for a pollution offence under CSA 2001 s. 191(2) is:
options: A fine of up to $5,000 only
A fine of up to $1,000,000, imprisonment up to 18 months, or both
A fine of up to $100,000 only
questions.explanation: Section 191(2) sets those limits. Section 192(2), for contravening directions, is $100,000, which is why the distractor is tempting.

questions.stem: Which of these is a factor a court may consider in sentencing under CSA 2001 s. 191(4)?
options: Whether the discharge or anticipated discharge was reported as required
questions.explanation: Section 191(4)(d) lists whether the discharge was reported, along with harm caused, clean-up costs, remedial action and history of non-compliance.
